newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr, RBI buys dollars.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr, RBI buys dollars.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended up against the spot dollar on Friday despite some late Reserve Bank of India (RBI) dollar purchases, dealers said.
They said the rupee ended at 35.805/815 against Thursday's close of 35.815/825. It opened Friday at 35.825/835.
Dealers said the rupee opened down on a statement on Thursday by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram that he would not like a stronger rupee.
"The rupee opened down in interbank trade but later on reverted to its now familiar mode of nudging up against the dollar," said a dealer.

"Had corporates reacted to Chidambaram's statement by covering their exposures, the rupee might have been under pressure," he said. "But this did not happen and the rupee rallied on strong dollar supply and poor demand."
The rupee has been buoyant in recent months on strong dollar inflows and poor demand and only RBI dollar purchases have kept it from appreciating sharply.
Dealers said the RBI bought dollars late Friday but were unsure of the amount. One dealer said the central bank bought spot dollars at 35.805 rupees and up to 35.81.
Dealers said the rupee ended Friday little changed against the forward dollar.
"Forward premiums opened higher from Thursday's close on expectations that importers would cover their exposures in reaction to Chidambaram's statement," said a dealer.
"But this did not happen and some selling at higher levels helped bring premiums down the day's highs," he said.
The annualised premium for six-month dollars ended Friday at 4.64 percent against Thursday's close of 4.58 percent.
